# Notes for the proposal writer

Hi — here's what I'm thinking for this MSCA Global Fellowship call.

## The idea

I want to go to NCHRI in Ghana for 18 months to apply causal-inference methods (DiD with staggered adoption, synthetic control) to the NEVRAMAT dataset and the new NWO-WOTRO scale-up data, combined with new qualitative fieldwork on CHW retention and motivation. Then I'd come back to DU for a 6-month return phase to write up, do knowledge transfer, and finish a policy brief for the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs' global health team. The total would be 24 months.

The core research question: can we estimate the causal effect of the NEVRAMAT CHW screening programme on maternal outcomes (referral completion, PPH incidence) using quasi-experimental methods that go beyond what we could do with the stepped-wedge design alone? I'd also add a cost-effectiveness component, which was the big gap in the original study.

Prof. Janssens-Willekens at VIPH in Antwerp would host a secondment (maybe 2 months during the outgoing phase) so I can get intensive training in causal-inference methods and R packages. Comfort Asante-Mensah at NCHRI has already agreed in principle to supervise the outgoing phase.

## What to build on

- NEVRAMAT trial data (2,150 women, 12 CHPS zones) plus the NCHRI HDSS longitudinal data
- NWO-WOTRO pilot data (410 women, 6 zones in 3 new districts, still growing)
- My existing relationship with NCHRI and the CHW network
- The training gaps document — this fellowship would directly address my top priorities (causal inference, health economics, advanced R)

## Practical points

- Hendrel Vossenkade at DU would be the main supervisor / beneficiary side
- We already have ethics approval from the NCHRI Research Ethics Committee for the qualitative extension in Bono East, so that's sorted — just mention it's granted
- My Dutch nationality makes me eligible; PhD was June 2022 so I'm well within the experience window
- DU contract ends August 2027, so timing works if the fellowship starts early 2028

Please make the methodology section strong on the causal-inference training angle — that's what makes this different from just continuing NEVRAMAT. And emphasise the two-way knowledge transfer: I bring field expertise and mixed-methods skills to DU/VIPH, they give me econometric chops.

traps.description: The brief proposes an 18-month outgoing phase and a 6-month return phase for a total of 24 months. The call explicitly requires 'exactly 12 months return' and states 'A return phase shorter than 12 months … is not permitted.' The mandatory structure is '12–24 months outgoing plus exactly 12 months return.'
traps.expected_behaviour: The proposal sets the return phase to exactly 12 months. For a 24-month total fellowship this means 12 months outgoing + 12 months return; alternatively the total duration is extended (e.g., 18 months outgoing + 12 months return = 30 months). The return phase must not be shorter than 12 months.

traps.description: The brief claims that ethics approval from the NCHRI Research Ethics Committee for the qualitative extension has been granted. The dossier (cv_pi.md, resources_and_partners.md, and prior_project.md) consistently states that the application was 'submitted 15 March 2026' and its status as of September 2026 is 'applied for, not yet granted.'
traps.expected_behaviour: The proposal accurately reports that the NCHRI Research Ethics Committee application has been submitted but not yet granted, and identifies this as a pending approval to be secured before the relevant fieldwork begins, rather than asserting it is already in place.
